RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone is not evidence of discrimination; in education, all-female panels frequently reflect organizational demographics rather than bias. Raising gender without concrete evidence will appear unsubstantiated, burning bridges and harming your professional reputation.

Once candidates reach the final shortlist, decisions typically hinge on interview performance, strategic vision, references, and institutional fit rather than paper qualifications alone. While subconscious bias is always a slight possibility in human evaluations, you currently have no proof that sex was a factor.

Instead of focusing on the panel’s gender, follow up politely on your request for written feedback. Ask for objective scoring rubrics and constructive notes to understand their decision and support future applications.
